title: Prove an overhead-crane stability interval
equipment: Overhead travelling crane trolley with suspended load
physicalPurpose: Establish the safe proportional-gain stability interval algebraically before hazardous time-domain trials.
objective: Derive the complete gain interval and predict stable, marginal, and unstable crane responses before executable confirmation.

simplifications: Local linear trolley and suspended-load dynamics
No structural flexibility or drive dynamics

baseline.limitation: A finite response at selected gains cannot prove the complete stability interval or expose a weakly excited unstable mode.

change.decision: Use the Routh first-column signs and independent numerical roots as authority; use equivalent time traces only as confirmation.

disturbances: Identical 0.1-metre initial displacement on each crane copy

acceptance.window: Routh array and independent roots before run
Routh array and independent roots before run
30-40 s peak absolute position divided by 2-12 s peak

abortPredicates: Any required signal is missing, stale, forced, nonfinite, or has bad quality
An individual trolley reaches two metres absolute position
An individual requested motor force exceeds 100 percent
Model identity, initial state, timing, gain, or limit differs from the reviewed experiment
safety.restorationMode: Disable the experiment, command zero motor force, and restart all three simulated models from the declared initial state
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised crane controls engineer and responsible lifting-equipment operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Never apply the marginal or unstable lesson gains to physical lifting equipment
Physical validation requires independently reviewed mechanics, topology, model, limits, interlocks, procedure, authorised roles, and explicit immediate approval

video.viewerOutcome: Derive a crane gain interval, classify the boundary, and use executable traces as confirmation rather than proof.

learning.context: Three equivalent simulated overhead-crane copies expose natural responses at proportional gains 4, 6, and 8.
learning.reason: Selected finite tuning runs cannot establish a complete stability interval or safely search for instability.
theory: Closed-loop poles are natural response modes whose real parts determine decay, persistence, or growth.
The Routh first-column sign changes count right-half-plane poles.
Zero first elements and complete zero rows require explicit special-case treatment.
learning.workedPrediction: Derive 0 < K < 6 and predict stable K=4, marginal K=6, and two unstable poles at K=8 before enabling simulation.
practicalPreparation: Verify identical models, initial displacement, zero setpoint, units, quality, timing, limits, aborts, restoration, and Simulation evidence.
Record the Routh table, numerical roots, and envelope criteria before the run.
learning.baseline: Finite time-domain inspection at selected gains cannot prove the full gain interval.
learning.change: Use Routh-Hurwitz and an independent root oracle before equivalent natural-response tests.
learning.comparison: Change only proportional gain while holding model, initial condition, timing, duration, limits, and seed equal.
learning.validation: Require algebra and roots to agree, then confirm decay, marginal persistence, and growth or safe abort in the executable plants.
learning.explanation: The sign of the s^1 first-column term changes at K=6, moving a pole pair from the left half-plane through the imaginary axis into the right half-plane.
learning.transfer: Routh proves an interval but not pole motion or acceptable damping; Lesson 46 introduces root locus.
